analyst_view.overall: Nice (7th, 17 pts) host Troyes (14th, 11 pts) on Saturday evening. Olivier Pantaloni's Nice lost 3-2 at home to PSG, ending a run of three wins, while promoted Troyes came from behind to beat bottom side Le Havre 3-1. Nice are missing Antoine Mendy, Laurent Abergel, Lumpungu and Bombito, with Abdelmonem working back to fitness; Troyes are without forward Yacoube Kone and defender Paolo Gozzi. These absences are weeks old and show in recent form, and none is a main scorer (Elye Wahi, Nice's top scorer with 6, is fit). Aurelien Petit referees (2.4 cards a game in five games), which the numbers already count; nothing beyond mid-table points is at stake, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Nice, who have scored 14 in their last six with Wahi fit to lead the line. Nice's patched defence has been patched for weeks and is in their form, and Troyes' loss of Kone is minor (Mille is their top scorer), so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, slightly more for Troyes, and momentum already trims both sides a little. Troyes see little of the ball (38% possession on average) but the numbers already know their style, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards: pushed up because Nice have had 17 cards in their last six, then trimmed about 11% for referee Aurelien Petit, who has shown only 2.4 a game. There is no rivalry or discipline news, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.9 shots, already trimmed because Troyes have allowed few shots lately and Nice have shot less than usual. Both sides are expected to field settled line-ups (about 85% of their XI kept over six games), so I stay at about 23.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, 4.6 for Nice. Nice's attack is intact and Troyes' defence has been tight lately (18 on target allowed in six), both already in the numbers, so I stay at about 8.
